title: MERGE Upsert with Concurrency Safety
description: Write an upsert that does not deadlock or duplicate rows under concurrent load.

data.text: Your application upserts customer rows with `MERGE`. Under load you occasionally see a primary key violation on insert, and sometimes a deadlock between two sessions running the same statement with different keys. Explain why this happens and write a version that is safe.

data.title: SQL Solution
data.code:
-- The classic MERGE upsert (has a known race: two sessions can both see 'not exists')
MERGE dbo.Customers AS target
USING (SELECT @CustomerId AS CustomerId, @Name AS Name, @Email AS Email) AS source
    ON target.CustomerId = source.CustomerId
WHEN MATCHED THEN
    UPDATE SET Name = source.Name, Email = source.Email
WHEN NOT MATCHED THEN
    INSERT (CustomerId, Name, Email) VALUES (source.CustomerId, source.Name, source.Email);
-- ...plus OPTION (HOLDLOCK) or an explicit transaction with the right isolation

-- Safer pattern: explicit transaction + HOLDLOCK serializable range lock on the key
BEGIN TRANSACTION;

UPDATE dbo.Customers
SET Name = @Name, Email = @Email
WHERE CustomerId = @CustomerId;

IF @@ROWCOUNT = 0
BEGIN
    BEGIN TRY
        INSERT INTO dbo.Customers (CustomerId, Name, Email)
        VALUES (@CustomerId, @Name, @Email);
    END TRY
    BEGIN CATCH
        -- Lost the race: another session inserted first, so update instead
        IF ERROR_NUMBER() = 2627   -- primary key violation
            UPDATE dbo.Customers
            SET Name = @Name, Email = @Email
            WHERE CustomerId = @CustomerId;
        ELSE
            THROW;
    END CATCH
END;

COMMIT TRANSACTION;

data.title: Explanation
data.text: MERGE evaluates its `WHEN NOT MATCHED` branch against a snapshot, so two concurrent sessions can both decide to insert the same key — one then fails with error 2627. `MERGE` also takes a range lock that can deadlock when sessions touch overlapping key ranges in different orders. The **update-then-insert-with-catch** pattern is easier to reason about: the UPDATE takes an exclusive lock on the row if it exists, and the primary key guarantees the insert cannot duplicate. If you keep MERGE, add `WITH (HOLDLOCK)` to the target to force serializable range locks, and always wrap it in an explicit transaction.
